name: Azshara
summary: Along northeastern Kalimdor, Azshara’s broken coast runs from autumn woods to drowned ruins and perilous waters. Horde and Alliance outposts stand near its borders, while naga, ghosts, and other dangers haunt the land.

sections.title: A Drowned Empire
sections.body: Zin-Azshari’s coast once lay at the heart of kaldorei civilization. Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara and her Highborne court drew the Burning Legion into Azeroth. So began the War of the Ancients. The Well of Eternity collapsed and the sea swallowed most of the magnificent city. Fractured cliffs, perilous coral reefs, and waterlogged spires remain. Survivors named the ruined land for their fallen monarch, whose pride and betrayal changed it forever.

sections.title: Autumn Splendor and Hidden Perils
sections.body: Crimson, orange, and gold leaves cover Azshara’s woods through an autumn that never ends. Yet the quiet canopy hides a harsh wilderness. Satyrs perform dark rituals in forest hollows, Highborne apparitions haunt drowned foundations, and Spitelash naga prowl the Coral Sea’s shallow reefs. Ferocious beasts, giant hydras, and mountain giants roam the highlands and ivory beaches.

sections.title: A Realm of Exiles and Outcasts
sections.body: Azshara’s isolation and harsh terrain draw those who pursue forgotten crafts or watch dangerous powers. Archmage Xylem lives in a secluded tower high above the cliffs. There, he tests promising spellcasters and cunning rogues. Farther along the coast, the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes watches the waves from a barren isle. At a temple above the churning waters, the immense sea giant Lord Arkkoroc demands blood sacrifices.

faq.q: Why are all the trees red and orange here?
faq.answer: Azshara’s woods wear crimson, orange, and gold leaves through an endless autumn. The canopy never sheds them, and this striking, melancholy sight has lasted for thousands of years.

faq.q: How did Azshara become a ruin?
faq.answer: The coast once formed the outskirts of Zin-Azshari, the kaldorei capital. During the War of the Ancients, the Well of Eternity imploded in the Great Sundering. The continent broke, and vast parts of the city sank beneath the sea.

Neither faction rules all of Azshara. The Alliance keeps a small watch at Talrendis Point near Ashenvale, and the Horde operates from Valormok. Dangerous Spitelash naga, violent satyrs, and untamed monsters dominate the surrounding land.

Archmage Xylem is an eccentric human sorcerer in a remote tower overlooking Azshara’s cliffs. He keeps apart from regional politics and guides visiting mages and rogues through trials that unlock their martial and arcane potential.

faq.q: What is the blue dragon doing in the ruins?
faq.answer: Azuregos and his brood watch over Eldarath’s ancient ruins. The great blue dragon fiercely guards the powerful Highborne magical artifacts buried in the rubble from mortal hands.

faq.q: Why do the night elves consider this land cursed?
aliases: why do night elves hate azshara
faq.answer: The kaldorei consider Azshara cursed because it bears Queen Azshara’s name and architectural legacy. Her pact with the Burning Legion shattered their empire and brought ruin to the world.

angles.text: As a night elf, you see drowned pillars and wailing Highborne shades. They recall Queen Azshara’s reckless arrogance and the ruin of the ancient kaldorei civilization.

As a mage, you find forgotten Highborne sorcery crackling through Eldarath’s shattered stones. High above the cliffs, Archmage Xylem tests those who seek mastery of arcane teleportation and spellcraft.
As a miner, you find precious veins in Azshara’s steep coastal cliffs and jagged ridges. Mithril, Truesilver, and Thorium are abundant.
As an herbalist, you find rare, potent herbs sustained by Azshara’s endless autumn. They include Dreamfoil, Golden Sansam, Mountain Silversage, and Purple Lotus among the ruins.
